rmt-2008-calc-01.title: Double angle
rmt-2008-calc-01.body:
$\sin x\cos x=\frac12\sin2x$, so the integral is $\frac12\left[-\frac12\cos2x\right]_0^{\pi/2}=\frac12\cdot\frac12(1+1)=\frac12$.

**Answer: $\frac12$**

rmt-2008-calc-02.title: L'Hopital twice
rmt-2008-calc-02.body:
Both numerator and denominator vanish at $0$. After the first derivative the limit is $\lim\frac{20x-\frac32x^2}{\frac23xe^{x^2/3}}$, still $\frac00$; after the second it is $\frac{20}{\frac23}=30$.

**Answer: 30**

rmt-2008-calc-03.title: Figure-eight
rmt-2008-calc-03.body:
The curve is a figure eight symmetric about both axes. For $0\le t\le\frac\pi2$, $x=\sin t\in[0,1]$ and $y=2\sin t\cos t=2x\sqrt{1-x^2}$, a quarter of the curve. The area under it is $\int_0^12x\sqrt{1-x^2}\,dx=\left[-\frac23(1-x^2)^{3/2}\right]_0^1=\frac23$. The whole figure is $4$ copies: $\frac83$.

**Answer: $\frac83$**

rmt-2008-calc-04.title: Product rule
rmt-2008-calc-04.body:
Write $f=\sin x\cdots\sin x$ ($n$ factors). The $n$th derivative is a sum over ways of distributing $n$ derivatives among the $n$ factors. Any term in which some factor is not differentiated still contains $\sin0=0$ at $x=0$, so only terms in which each factor is differentiated exactly once survive; each equals $\cos^n0=1$, and there are $n!$ of them (the order in which the factors receive their derivatives).

**Answer: $n!$**

rmt-2008-calc-05.title: Differential equation
rmt-2008-calc-05.body:
The volume is $w(t)=100+t$ gallons. The salt $s(t)$ leaves at the rate $2\frac{s}{w}$, so $\frac{ds}{dt}=-\frac{2s}{100+t}$. Separating variables, $\ln s=-2\ln(100+t)+C$, so $s=\frac{C'}{(100+t)^2}$. From $s(0)=50$, $C'=500000$. At $t=60$: $s=\frac{500000}{160^2}=\frac{625}{32}\approx19.5$ pounds.

**Answer: $\frac{625}{32}$ pounds**

rmt-2008-calc-06.title: Integrate by parts twice
rmt-2008-calc-06.body:
Let $I=\int e^{3x}\sin x\,dx$. Then $I=\frac13e^{3x}\sin x-\frac13\int e^{3x}\cos x\,dx=\frac13e^{3x}\sin x-\frac13\left(\frac13e^{3x}\cos x+\frac13\int e^{3x}\sin x\,dx\right)$, so $I=\frac13e^{3x}\sin x-\frac19e^{3x}\cos x-\frac19I$. Hence $\frac{10}9I=\frac{e^{3x}}9(3\sin x-\cos x)$ and $I=\frac{e^{3x}}{10}(3\sin x-\cos x)+C$.

**Answer: $\frac{e^{3x}}{10}(3\sin x-\cos x)+C$**

rmt-2008-calc-08.title: Second difference
rmt-2008-calc-08.body:
$f(x+2h)-2f(x+h)+f(x)=f''(x)h^2+o(h^2)$, so the limit is $\frac1{f''(x)}$. Thus $f''(x)=\frac1{-\frac{x^3}2-x-\frac1{2x}}=-\frac{2x}{x^4+2x^2+1}=-\frac{2x}{(1+x^2)^2}$. Integrating, $f'(x)=\frac1{1+x^2}+a$ and $f(x)=\tan^{-1}x+ax+b$.

**Answer: $f(x)=\tan^{-1}x+ax+b$**

rmt-2008-calc-09.title: Match coefficients
rmt-2008-calc-09.body:
$x''=\sum n(n-1)a_nt^{n-2}$, $x'=\sum na_nt^{n-1}=\sum(n-1)a_{n-1}t^{n-2}$ (shifting the index), and $t^5x=\sum a_{n-7}t^{n-2}$ (shifting by $7$). Comparing the coefficients of $t^{n-2}$: $n(n-1)a_n+(n-1)a_{n-1}=a_{n-7}$, so $a_n=\frac{a_{n-7}-(n-1)a_{n-1}}{n(n-1)}$.

**Answer: $a_n=\frac{a_{n-7}-(n-1)a_{n-1}}{n(n-1)}$**

rmt-2008-calc-10.title: Integration by parts
rmt-2008-calc-10.body:
$2^te^t=(2e)^t$ and $\int(2e)^tdt=\frac{(2e)^t}{c}$ with $c=\ln(2e)=1+\ln2$. By parts, $\int t(2e)^tdt=\frac{t(2e)^t}c-\frac1c\int(2e)^tdt=\frac{t(2e)^t}c-\frac{(2e)^t}{c^2}$. As $t\to-\infty$ both terms tend to $0$ (since $2e>1$), so the integral from $-\infty$ to $x$ is $(2e)^x\left(\frac x{1+\ln2}-\frac1{(1+\ln2)^2}\right)$.

**Answer: $(2e)^x\left(\frac{x}{1+\ln2}-\frac1{(1+\ln2)^2}\right)$**
